The Software Engineer - AI & Security Technology is responsible for designing, developing, implementing, and supporting technology solutions that enable and enhance Physical Corporate Security operations. This role combines software engineering, AI/automation, reporting and analytics, database administration, and infrastructure support to improve security operations, access control, visitor management, video surveillance, executive protection, threat intelligence, and incident management capabilities.
The successful candidate will develop custom applications, AI-powered solutions, integrations, dashboards, and automation workflows while supporting enterprise security platforms, databases, servers, and cloud-based services.
Remote: You'll enjoy the flexibility to telecommute* from anywhere within the U.S. as you take on some tough challenges.
Primary Responsibilities
Support and maintain enterprise corporate security platforms including: Access Control, Visitor Management Video Surveillance Systems, Alarm Monitoring Platforms, Risk Intelligence and Command Center systems
Design, develop, enhance, and support software integrations between security systems, enterprise applications, and cloud services
Develop and maintain applications, APIs, databases, automation scripts, and reporting solutions that improve security operations and business processes
Support AI-driven security initiatives including video analytics, threat detection, automation, reporting, and operational intelligence solutions
Troubleshoot application, server, database, and integration issues and coordinate resolution of production incidents affecting corporate security operations

payload.text:
I assumed AWS Local Zone in Lagos was the easy answer to the CBN localisation requirement. Then I sat down and read the documentation properly.

It isn't, at least not for the data layer.

There's no RDS in the Lagos Local Zone, so you'd be self-managing Postgres or MySQL on EC2. Also, Local Zones extend a parent Region (Lagos is linked to af-south-1), so EBS snapshots write to S3 in the parent Region by default. Local snapshots only work in Local Zones with S3 in-zone, and Lagos doesn't have that. So your backups end up in Cape Town.

Which leads to the bigger problem. There's no AWS Region in Nigeria. No Azure Region or Google Cloud Region either. If your payment database runs on a hyperscaler today, it's sitting in Ireland, Virginia or Cape Town — and so are your automated backups and your KMS keys.

The June circular requires payment transaction data generated in Nigeria to be stored and managed in Nigeria from 1 January 2027. That's under 90 days. For most teams, this isn't a settings change, because there's nowhere to point it at.

The harder question is what "𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐍𝐢𝐠𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐚" actually means in practice. Several law firms read it as covering the primary processing environment rather than just a copy held locally, which would mean backing up from a hyperscaler into Nigeria doesn't meet it. I put that question to Huawei Cloud directly and got the same answer, though they'd obviously have an interest in saying so.

I've been working out how Nigerian startups can meet these requirements without needing a large infrastructure team or building everything from scratch.

If you're working through this at a Nigerian fintech or building infrastructure for one, I'd be glad to compare notes.

#Fintech #Nigeria #CloudComputing #AWS

⚡ NordPSA 2.0: ny Nordenmodell, nya svar

Sedan i juni har jag byggt om den öppna Nordenmodellen #NordPSA rejält, och kört om både baseline 2040 och jämförelsen med Svenska kraftnäts LMA26 (Mixat Medel). Resultatet finns nu i tre bloggposter.

Det viktigaste som ändrats i modellen:
🔹Samma körsätt som SvK: 2h-expansion följd av 1h-drift med begränsad framsyn.
🔹Vattenkraften budar efter ett vattenvärde, inte efter historiska priser, och är kalibrerad mot hur den verkliga vattenkraften svarar på priset. Den visar sig vara betydligt trögare än jag antagit tidigare.
🔹Krav på tröghet ("rotationsenergi") och nätstyrka ("kortslutningseffekt"), flexibel vätgas och efterfrågeflex enligt LMA26.

1. Baseline 2040  〰️ 
Den trögare vattenkraften gör solel mindre värd: 16 GW mindre sol, mer havsvind i Norge. Priserna hamnar några euro högre. Vattenkraften balanserar mindre av dygnets svängningar, och elbilar och batterier tar över.

2. LMA26 MM, Del 1: stabilitet och energibalans  ⚖️ 
Sveriges energibalans stämmer väl med LMA26. Kraven på tröghet och nätstyrka klaras varje timme för cirka 160 M€/år. Det är nätstyrkan, och inte trögheten, som är den bindande bristen, men den befintliga kärnkraften gör den relativt billig.

3. LMA26 MM, Del 2: prisbildning  💰 
Lager sätter priset: vattenkraften i ungefär hälften av timmarna, batterier och elbilsladdning i 10–18 %. De dyraste timmarna sätts av förbrukning som avstår. Vanliga timmar blir dyrare, men de extrema topparna försvinner. Flera grafiska exempel (utbud/efterfrågan) på nordisk prisbildning ges och förklaras.

Länkar i första kommentaren.

#energi #elmarknad #kraftsystem #vattenkraft #elpris #energimodellering #PyPSA

China produces about 85% of the world's cathode active material. The West needs new battery chemistries to compete, but traditional R&D can take years to deliver them. 
 
Today, we announced $45M in funding to change that. 
 
Backed by  Zone II Ventures, and Course Corrected, we're scaling our AI-powered Discovery Engine, which combines 18 years of proprietary battery data with automated labs that physically build and test new materials. Over these 18 years our platform has run more than 225 projects for more than 85 customers across the battery value chain, including nearly a dozen Fortune 500 companies, and has resulted in more than 100 battery patents.  Along the way, the platform generated an internally consistent dataset covering more than 500,000 physical cells tested at over 165 million cycles.  
 
Our technology has already helped deliver DRX, a new family of nickel- and cobalt-free cathode materials designed to reduce dependence on China. Now, we're bringing DRX toward commercialization while using AI to accelerate the next generation of breakthroughs. 
 
Led by founder and CEO Mathias Ingvarsson, COO and former Tesla manufacturing leader Steven Prast, and Chief Scientific Officer Dee Strand, we're building a faster path from battery discovery to commercial deployment. 
 
Read more in Fortune by Nick Lichtenberg. Article link in the first comment.

XBOX is building a new kind of flywheel with games at the center.

The company announced XP this morning (a clever title)—a new division headed by Kayleen Walters focused on creating more on-ramps for fans to its beloved IP through film & television, consumer products, live events, and strategic partnerships.

Here are the four divisions:

* XBOX PICTURES: Bringing our worlds and characters to new audiences through film, television, and other forms of linear storytelling. 
* XBOX PRODUCTS: Creating products that are authentic to the fandom that allow fans to celebrate and express the franchises they love. 
* XBOX PLACES: Bringing communities together through live events, immersive experiences, attractions, broadcasts, and destinations. 
* XBOX PARTNERSHIPS: Working with creators, brands, and communities to develop new experiences, sponsorships, and brand partnerships.

The move—championed by Matthew Ball following an internal memo from Asha Sharma—is both elegant and strategic. It adopts the best strategies from Disney and Nintendo, both of whom understand that content is king. Where Disney’s flywheel was built strategically around film and television firs, Nintendo’s is game first.

With this move, XBOX is positioning itself to move beyond being a mere platform to owning its market position as both a publisher and steward of massive IP (from Minecraft to Halo and beyond).

I’m excited to see where this leads.

Game studio funding is back: Gardens Interactive has raised a $35M+ Series B, bringing total funding to over $70M before launching its flagship game.

Led by Lightspeed, the round includes Sequoia Capital, Index Ventures, Accel, Eric Schmidt’s Innovation Endeavors, the Nintendo family (Yamauchi No.10), the ZeniMax Media family (James Altman), and the founders of Slack and OpenAI's Sora.

By any measure, but certainly in 2026, that's an extraordinary vote of confidence and tier-1 syndicate for a pre-launch studio. What inspires that conviction while it seems all venture dollars chase automation?

A team creating a new genre around a simple and proven design principle: deepen human connections, and let the players be the fun.

Gardens calls it a “strandbox”: a social roleplaying world where chance encounters become adventures, players shape each other’s stories, and your actions leave something behind for whoever comes next.

From serial game-of-the-year creators behind Journey and Sky, the team blends indie creativity and beautiful art with an ambitious AAA live-ops platform bet on how games can create significant and long-lasting emotional encounters.

This one is deeply personal. I love Stephen, 🔔Chris, and Lexie like brothers. After serving on Gardens’ board for the past three years, I’m rejoining as a personal investor and advisor, doubling down with my own capital and time. To continue an extraordinary development journey that already brought so many wonderful once-strangers together.

I can’t wait for you all to play what they’re building.
